body:
Chrome extensions running on `chrome-extension://` pages can only
reliably intercept **bare keys with no modifiers**. Every `⌘`, `Ctrl`,
and `Alt` combo we tried is claimed by Chrome at the browser level:

- `⌘1–9` / `Alt+1–9` / `Ctrl+Tab` / `Ctrl+Shift+Tab` / `⌘⇧]` / `⌘⇧[` /
  `⌘W` all switch Chrome's own tabs, not ours.
- `preventDefault()` in page JS cannot override browser-level chords.

Current scheme (all gated on `!isInInput(e)` so typing is safe):

| Chord | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `]` | next tab |
| `[` | prev tab |
| `x` | close active tab |
| `1`–`9` | jump to tab N |
| `f` | fullscreen |
| `r` | rendered ↔ raw |
| `\` | toggle TOC |
| `/` | focus folder filter |
| `⌘K` | search (Chrome leaves `⌘K` alone) |
| `⌘B` | toggle sidebar (Chrome leaves this too) |
| `Esc` | close overlays / exit fullscreen |

Every chord maps to a `ShortcutId` in `settings.ts` → togglable per-
shortcut on the options page. Master "Disable all shortcuts" flag in
the same store.
